mainTopic: An אונן and holy offerings: touching versus eating, eating קדשים at night, and רבי שמעון's view that night אנינות is rabbinic
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא: a man watched his basket but not the shovel inside it, so the basket is טהור and the shovel is טמא. The גמרא explains that a כלי does not make another כלי טמא. רבא adds that the shovel was guarded from passing on impurity, so the food in the basket stays pure. Next, רבי אבא בר ממל settles an earlier contradiction about an אונן: the Rabbis made an extra rule (מעלה) for eating קדשים but not for touching them. The גמרא then reads our משנה to mean that an אונן may eat קדשים at night if others invite him. It asks why a משנה in פסחים seems to say otherwise. רב ירמיה מדיפתי answers that our משנה is about פסח night. רב אסי answers that it depends on which day the relative died, because a burial day does not carry into its night מדרבנן. That answer follows רבי שמעון, who holds that night אנינות is only rabbinic. The גמרא then challenges him from his own ברייתא, which lists the פסח among offerings an אונן may not bring. רב חסדא and רב ששת each answer, and רב מרי begins a third answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The basket stays pure but the shovel becomes impure
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא: a man was attentive to the basket but not to the shovel inside it, so the basket is טהור and the shovel is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and a shovel was inside the basket, and he said: 'I am paying attention to the basket, but I am not paying attention to the shovel.' The basket is pure, and the shovel is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the last lines of a ברייתא. A man guarded a basket from impurity but said he was not watching the shovel inside it, so only the basket stays pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Purity here depends on what the person was paying attention to. Because he was watching the basket, it stays טהור. Because he was not watching the shovel, it is treated as טמא, even though the two were together.

keyTerms.meaning: A shovel or scoop
A basket
Literally 'my heart is on': I am paying attention to, guarding
Ritually pure / ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא actually starts before this point. These words are only its ending, so 'inside it' means inside the basket that was already mentioned.

phrases.english: and a shovel was inside it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the basket from the start of the ברייתא, which began just before this point.

phrases.english: and he said: 'My heart is on the basket,'
phrases.notes: 'My heart is on' means 'I'm keeping an eye on it' so it stays pure.

phrases.english: 'but my heart is not on the shovel' –
the basket is pure, and the shovel is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַגְרֵיפָה בְּתוֹכוֹ, וְאָמַר: לִבִּי עַל הַסַּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that began in the text before this point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a person is attentive to the basket but not to the shovel inside it, the basket is טהור and the shovel is טמא.

steps.title: Shouldn't the shovel make the basket impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since the impure shovel is inside the basket, why doesn't it make the basket impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the shovel make the basket impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. If the shovel is impure and it sits inside the basket, how can the basket stay pure?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling seems to ignore contact. Normally a טמא object touching something can pass its impurity on, so the basket should become impure too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But let it make impure!' The גמרא uses this form to ask why something should not happen

phrases.english: But let the shovel make the basket impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 1 that the basket stays pure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the basket is טהור although the impure shovel is inside it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An impure object touching another object should make it impure, so the basket should be טמא.

steps.title: A vessel does not make another vessel impure
steps.stepSummary: Answer: a כלי does not make another כלי טמא, so the shovel cannot make the basket impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: A vessel does not make a vessel impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a known rule: one כלי cannot pass impurity to another כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shovel and the basket are both כלים. Since a כלי does not make another כלי טמא, the basket stays pure and the ברייתא's ruling holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel does not make another vessel impure
A vessel or utensil

phrases.english: A vessel does not make a vessel impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a general rule of impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The impure shovel should pass its impurity to the basket.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כלי cannot make another כלי טמא, so the basket stays טהור.

steps.title: Shouldn't the shovel make the food inside impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further: even if the basket stays pure, the shovel should make the food inside the basket impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it make impure what is inside the basket!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second question. The rule about כלים does not protect food, so why doesn't the shovel make the food in the basket impure?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'a כלי does not make a כלי טמא' only covers other vessels. Food can become impure from a כלי, so the contents of the basket seem to be in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: What is inside it: the food in the basket

phrases.english: But let it make impure what is inside it!
phrases.notes: The shovel should make the food in the basket impure, figs for example.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 3 but raises a new problem about the food.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the shovel's impurity causes no further harm.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule about כלים does not cover food, so the impure shovel should make the food in the basket impure.

steps.title: רבא: he guarded the shovel from spreading impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the man guarded the shovel from anything that would let it make other things impure. He only failed to guard it from what makes the shovel itself unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The case is where he says: 'I guarded it from anything that would make it pass on impurity, but I did not guard it from anything that makes it unfit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the second question by explaining exactly what the man meant. The shovel's impurity stays with the shovel and does not spread to the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of care. The man did guard the shovel from the kind of impurity that would let it pass impurity on, so the food is safe. He did not guard it from becoming unfit itself, which is why the ברייתא calls the shovel impure.

keyTerms.meaning: I guarded it
Something that would let it make other things impure
Something that makes it unfit (impure) itself

steps.whatToRemember: The basket is safe because a כלי does not make a כלי טמא. The food is safe because the shovel was guarded from anything that would let it spread impurity. Only the shovel itself is unfit.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is where he says: I guarded it from anything that would make it impart impurity,
but I did not guard it from anything that makes it unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּאוֹמֵר שְׁמַרְתִּיהָ מִדָּבָר הַמְטַמְּאָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case more narrowly (what the man said)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The impure shovel should make the food in the basket impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: He guarded the shovel from things that would let it spread impurity, so only the shovel itself is unfit and the food stays pure.

steps.title: רבי אבא בר ממל cites the rule of one who ate שלישי of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The question about the אונן reaches רבי אבא בר ממל. He points to רבי יוחנן's report in the name of רבי: one who ate third-degree תרומה may not eat תרומה but may touch it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter traveled around and came before רבי אבא בר ממל. He said to them: Haven't they heard what רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי: One who eats תרומה of third-degree impurity is forbidden to eat תרומה but allowed to touch it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier contradiction about an אונן: our משנה lets him touch קדשים, but the משנה in חגיגה requires him to immerse. רבי אבא בר ממל brings a known ruling as a model for solving it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cited ruling treats eating and touching differently. A person who ate שלישי of תרומה becomes unfit to eat תרומה, yet he may still touch it. That gives a pattern for the אונן case.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter traveled around (was passed from one scholar to another)
Third degree of impurity
The portion of produce given to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about the basket anymore. The גמרא has gone back to the older question about an אונן touching versus eating קדשים.

phrases.english: The matter traveled around,
phrases.notes: 'The matter' is the earlier contradiction about an אונן, not the basket case.

phrases.aramaic: וּמְטַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל.
phrases.english: and it came before Rabbi Abba bar Memel.
He said to them: Have they not heard

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: that which Rabbi Yoḥanan said that Rabbi said:
One who eats third-degree teruma –
phrases.notes: He means תרומה that got the third level of impurity by touching something second-level.

phrases.english: is forbidden to eat, but permitted to touch?
phrases.notes: He may not eat תרומה afterward, but he may still touch it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיגַּלְגַּל מִילְּתָא, וּמְטַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the basket discussion and goes back to the earlier contradiction about the אונן.
steps.raayaObject: That the Rabbis' extra strictness can apply to eating without applying to touching.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי: one who ate שלישי of תרומה may not eat תרומה but may touch it.

steps.title: Extra strictness for eating, not for touching
steps.stepSummary: From the cited ruling, the Rabbis made a מעלה for eating but not for touching. That solves the contradiction about the אונן.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see: for eating, the Rabbis made an extra strictness; for touching, the Rabbis did not make an extra strictness!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל draws the lesson from רבי's ruling. He uses it to answer the contradiction: the אונן must immerse before eating קדשים, but not before touching them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in חגיגה, which requires immersion, is talking about eating. Our משנה, which allows touching, is talking about touching. Since the Rabbis' extra rule covers only eating, the two משניות do not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see / apparently
An extra level of strictness set by the Rabbis
Eating / touching
The Rabbis made (enacted)

steps.whatToRemember: The Rabbis' extra strictness (מעלה) applies to eating holy food but not to touching it. That is why an אונן may touch קדשים but must immerse before eating them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the contradiction between our משנה and the משנה in חגיגה. Both are right, because each is talking about a different action.

phrases.english: Apparently, in eating the Rabbis made a higher standard,
in touching the Rabbis did not make a higher standard!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the ruling cited in step 6 and applies it to the אונן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: eating versus touching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות contradict each other about whether an אונן needs immersion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Immersion (the מעלה) is required for eating קדשים, not for touching them, so both משניות are correct.

steps.title: Reading our משנה closely: an אונן cannot take a share, but may eat if invited
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה, which says an אונן does not take a share of קדשים to eat at night. It learns from the exact wording that he may still eat if other כהנים invite him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And he does not take a share to eat, etc.' This means only that he may not take his own share. But when others invite him to join their portions, he eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in our משנה about the אונן and reads its exact wording carefully. This sets up the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says he does not take a share. It does not say he cannot eat. So the גמרא learns that eating itself is allowed at night when he joins someone else's portion.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day a close relative died, before burial. He may not eat קדשים during that day.
Takes a share. Here it means getting his own portion of the sacrificial meat.
They invite him to join in their portion.
Short for 'etc.' The rest of the quoted line continues.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'taking a share' with 'eating.' The גמרא is saying the משנה forbids only the first. The second is still allowed if he is invited.

phrases.english: And he does not take a share to eat, etc.
It is taking a share that he does not do,
but when they invite him, he eats;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The גמרא returns to another line of the משנה after finishing the discussion about the אונן touching versus eating קדשים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונן may not take his own share of קדשים, but at night he may eat them if others invite him.

steps.title: A משנה in פסחים says an אונן eats only his פסח, not other קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה from פסחים. It says an אונן immerses and eats his קרבן פסח at night, but not other קדשים. That seems to clash with what we just learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: An אונן immerses and eats his פסח in the evening, but not other קדשים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 8 with a משנה in פסחים. That משנה seems to forbid an אונן from eating any קדשים except the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said an אונן may eat קדשים at night if invited. The משנה in פסחים allows only the פסח and says 'but not קדשים.' So the two משניות seem to disagree about whether an אונן may eat other קדשים at night.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contradicted it. This is the formula for bringing a source that clashes with the one we just learned.
Immerses in a מקוה.
His קרבן פסח.
Sacrificial meat.

phrases.english: And they contradicted this:
phrases.notes: The source quoted next is a משנה in פסחים.

phrases.english: An acute mourner (and one who still needs to bring his atonement offering)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The question here is only about the אונן.

phrases.english: immerses and eats his Pesach offering in the evening,
but not other sacrificial meat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading from step 8 with a contradicting משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading from step 8 that an אונן may eat קדשים at night when invited.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in פסחים allows an אונן to eat only the פסח and says outright 'but not קדשים.' That clashes with allowing him to eat קדשים when invited.

steps.title: רב ירמיה מדיפתי: one source is about פסח, the other about the rest of the year
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה מדיפתי says the two משניות do not disagree. Our משנה is talking about the night of פסח, and the משנה in פסחים is talking about the rest of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה from דיפתי said: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about פסח, and there it is talking about the rest of the days of the year.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה מדיפתי answers the contradiction by saying each משנה is talking about a different time of year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה, which lets the invited אונן eat קדשים, is about the night of פסח. The משנה in פסחים, which says 'not קדשים,' is about every other day of the year. Since each source covers a different time, they no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is how an answer that settles a contradiction begins.
Here... there. Each source is talking about a different case.
The rest of the days of the year.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya of Difti said:
It is not difficult;
here, it is about Pesach,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our משנה, which lets him eat when invited. It is talking about the night of פסח.

phrases.english: there, it is about the rest of the days of the year.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן בְּפֶסַח, כָּאן בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different time of year.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seem to be about the same situation, so they appear to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about the night of פסח, and the משנה in פסחים is about the rest of the year.

steps.title: Why פסח is different, and what 'but not קדשים' really means
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה explains his answer. On פסח, since the אונן is already eating the פסח, he may eat other קדשים too. During the rest of the year he is unfit. 'But not קדשים' in פסחים means 'not קדשים of the rest of the year.'
steps.simpleTranslation: On פסח, since he eats the פסח, he also eats other קדשים. During the rest of the year, when he is unfit, he is unfit. And what does 'but not קדשים' mean? It means: but not קדשים of all the rest of the year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the night of פסח is different from the rest of the year. It then shows how to read the words 'but not קדשים' in the משנה in פסחים so they fit the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On פסח night the אונן is already allowed to eat the פסח, so he is allowed to eat other קדשים along with it. On other days nothing allows him to eat, so he stays unfit. The phrase 'but not קדשים' is not a ban for פסח night. It refers to קדשים on all the other days of the year.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, or because. One thing is allowed, so the thing that comes with it is allowed too.
He is not fit.
And what does it mean? The גמרא is asking how to read a phrase.

steps.whatToRemember: An אונן may eat קדשים at night only on the night of פסח, because he is already eating the פסח. During the rest of the year he may not. That is why our משנה (פסח night, eating when invited) and the משנה in פסחים (the rest of the year, 'not קדשים') do not contradict each other.

phrases.english: On Pesach, since he eats the Pesach offering,
he also eats other sacrificial meat.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה – דְּלָא חֲזֵי, לָא חֲזֵי.
phrases.english: During the rest of the days of the year, when he is unfit, he is unfit.
And what does 'but not other sacrificial meat' mean?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the words of the משנה in פסחים from step 9.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא בְּקָדָשִׁים שֶׁל כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה.
phrases.english: It means: but not sacrificial meat of all the rest of the year.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפֶסַח – אַיְּידֵי דְּאָכֵיל פֶּסַח, אָכֵיל נָמֵי קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the split in step 10 and reads the words of the משנה in פסחים to fit it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reasoning and rereads the wording of the opposing source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'but not קדשים' seem to forbid קדשים even on the night of פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words mean קדשים on the rest of the year. On פסח night, eating the פסח lets the אונן eat other קדשים too.

steps.title: רב אסי: It depends on which day the relative died
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי offers a different answer. In one משנה the relative died and was buried on the 14th. In the other he died on the 13th and was buried on the 14th, and a burial day does not carry over to its night מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: There is no contradiction. In one case the relative died on the 14th and was buried on the 14th. In the other case he died on the 13th and was buried on the 14th. A day of burial does not take hold of its night, by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives a second way to settle the clash between the two משניות. He says they are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the relative died on the 14th, the אנינות of the day of death carries into the night מדרבנן, so the אונן may not eat קדשים (the משנה in פסחים). If he died on the 13th and was only buried on the 14th, the burial day does not carry into the night, so he may eat (our משנה). Unlike רב ירמיה, this answer splits the cases by the day of death, not by פסח night versus the rest of the year.

keyTerms.meaning: The day of burial
Takes hold of its night, meaning the status carries into the following night
By rabbinic law, not by Torah law
It is not difficult: there is no real contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two days. Death and burial on the same day (the 14th) means NO קדשים that night. Death on the 13th with burial on the 14th means he MAY eat.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said: It is not difficult;

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן שֶׁמֵּת לוֹ מֵת בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
phrases.english: here, it is where his relative died on the fourteenth
and he buried him on the fourteenth,
phrases.notes: This first case is the משנה in פסחים, where he may not eat other קדשים that night.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן שֶׁמֵּת לוֹ מֵת בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר
phrases.english: there, it is where his relative died on the thirteenth
and he buried him on the fourteenth;

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם קְבוּרָה לָא תָּפֵיס לֵילוֹ מִדְּרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: a day of burial does not take hold of its night by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of Step 9, as an alternative to רב ירמיה's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases (אוקימתא by day of death)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seem to contradict each other about whether an אונן may eat קדשים at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה in פסחים covers death and burial on the 14th. Our משנה covers death on the 13th and burial on the 14th, and a burial day does not carry over to its night מדרבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer assumes that night אנינות is only rabbinic, which leads straight into the next question: who holds that?

steps.title: Who holds that night mourning is only rabbinic?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that אנינות at night is only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that acute mourning at night is by rabbinic law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask whose opinion רב אסי's answer is based on. It is setting up the next step, which names the תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי's answer depends on the idea that night אנינות is only מדרבנן. The גמרא wants a תנא who actually says that.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (the Sage of the משנה era) who holds this?
The status of acute mourning during the night

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who holds that acute mourning at night is by rabbinic law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the assumption behind רב אסי's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that night אנינות is only rabbinic.

steps.title: It is רבי שמעון, who argues with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: It is רבי שמעון. A ברייתא records רבי יהודה saying night אנינות is Torah law and רבי שמעון saying it is rabbinic. רבי שמעון proves this from the fact that an אונן eats his פסח at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי שמעון, as a ברייתא teaches: Acute mourning at night is by Torah law; these are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון says: An אונן at night is not by Torah law but by rabbinic law. Know that this is so, because they said: An אונן immerses and eats his פסח in the evening, but not other קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the opinion belongs to רבי שמעון, and brings a ברייתא where he argues with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that night אנינות is Torah law. רבי שמעון holds it is only rabbinic. His proof: the אונן is allowed to eat the פסח at night, which could not be allowed if night אנינות were Torah law. He still may not eat other קדשים, because the rabbis were strict about those.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
By the words of the scribes, meaning rabbinic law
Know that this is so: introduces a proof
Immerses in a מקוה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says night אנינות is Torah law. רבי שמעון says it is rabbinic, and proves it from the אונן eating his פסח at night.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon.
As it is taught in a baraita: Acute mourning at night is by Torah law.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אוֹנֵן אֵינוֹ מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: An acute mourner is not by Torah law,
phrases.notes: He means being an אונן at night, after the day of death.

phrases.english: but by rabbinic law.
Know that this is so, as they said:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹנֵן טוֹבֵל וְאוֹכֵל אֶת פִּסְחוֹ לָעֶרֶב,
phrases.english: An acute mourner immerses and eats his Paschal offering in the evening,
phrases.notes: This is the same משנה from פסחים that came up in Step 9.

phrases.english: but not other sacrificial meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון, who holds in a ברייתא that night אנינות is rabbinic, against רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי שמעון says an אונן does not send his offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי שמעון really holds that night אנינות is rabbinic. Another ברייתא quotes him saying an אונן does not send his offerings, which seems to include even the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון really hold that night אנינות is rabbinic? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, an אונן does not send his offerings. Does this not mean even the פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי שמעון holds night אנינות is rabbinic, using a different ברייתא in his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an אונן may not even send his פסח to be offered, he would not be eating it at night either. That would clash with רבי שמעון's own proof that an אונן eats his פסח in the evening.

keyTerms.meaning: Sends his offerings to the Temple to be brought
What, is it not...? A suggested reading used to press a challenge

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֲנִינוּת לַיְלָה מִדְּרַבָּנַן?!
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Shimon hold that acute mourning at night is by rabbinic law?!
But isn't it taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon says:
An acute mourner does not send his offerings.
What, is it not even with a Paschal offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֲנִינוּת לַיְלָה מִדְּרַבָּנַן? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in Step 14 that רבי שמעון holds night אנינות is rabbinic.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון holds night אנינות is only rabbinic, so an אונן eats his פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא has רבי שמעון saying an אונן does not send his offerings. That seems to include the פסח, which contradicts his ruling that an אונן eats his פסח at night.

steps.title: No: it means offerings other than the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means all offerings except the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means other than the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing what the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Does not send his offerings" refers to all other offerings, not the פסח. So רבי שמעון can still hold that an אונן brings and eats his פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Other than the פסח: excluding it

phrases.english: No; it is other than a Paschal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: "His offerings" means all offerings except the פסח.

steps.title: Another challenge: "שלמים" means only when he is whole
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא of רבי שמעון. From the word שלמים, it learns that a person brings it when he is שלם, not when he is an אונן. The תודה is included because it too is eaten with joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, "שלמים": when he is whole he brings it, and he does not bring it when he is an אונן. From where do we include the תודה? I include the תודה because it is eaten with joy, like שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא of רבי שמעון to press the challenge again. It quotes the whole ברייתא first, through step 19. Step 20 points out the problem, and step 21 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reads the word שלמים as "שלם" (whole): an אונן, who is not whole, does not bring it. He then extends the rule to the תודה because it is eaten with joy. As the ברייתא goes on, it will name the פסח too, and that explicit mention is what the challenge in step 20 is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings
Whole: at peace and content, not in mourning
Thanksgiving offering
To include: to extend a rule to another case
Joy

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon says:
"Peace offerings": when he is whole, he brings it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:1. He reads שלמים as if it says שלם, "whole."

phrases.english: and he does not bring it when he is an acute mourner.
From where do we include the thanks offering?
I include the thanks offering,
since it is eaten with joy like a peace offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the challenge against רבי שמעון's view, after Step 16 answered the first challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that רבי שמעון holds an אונן brings and eats his פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This second ברייתא of רבי שמעון goes on (step 18) to name the פסח outright among the offerings an אונן may not bring. So the answer of step 16, that 'his offerings' means everything except the פסח, cannot work here. The גמרא states the challenge in step 20, and רב חסדא answers it in step 21.

steps.title: The ברייתא includes the עולה, בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת and אשם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues and extends the rule beyond שלמים. The עולה is included because it is voluntary like שלמים. בכור, מעשר and פסח are included because they do not atone for sin. חטאת and אשם are included from the word זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know the עולה is also included? I include it, because like שלמים it can come as a נדר or as a נדבה. How do we know בכור, מעשר and פסח are included? I include them, because like שלמים they do not come for a sin. How do we know חטאת and אשם are included? The verse says 'זבח'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא from step 17. It adds more and more kinds of offerings that an אונן may not bring. This is setting up the challenge that comes in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each new offering is included because it shares some feature with שלמים. The עולה shares being voluntary. בכור, מעשר and פסח share not being brought for a sin. חטאת and אשם share nothing like that, so they need the extra word זבח. Notice that פסח is on this list. That is what the גמרא will soon pick on.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering, burned entirely on the מזבח
Two kinds of voluntary offerings. A נדר is a pledge in general, and a נדבה is a specific animal set aside
Firstborn animal offering
Animal tithe offering, every tenth animal
A slaughtered offering. Here it includes every animal offering

phrases.english: From where do we include the burnt offering?
I include the burnt offering,
since it comes as a vow and as a gift, like a peace offering.
From where do we include firstborn, tithe and Pesach?
I include firstborn, tithe and Pesach,
since they do not come for a sin.
From where do we include sin and guilt offerings?
The verse says: 'a sacrifice.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:1, 'זבח שלמים'. The word זבח stretches the rule to any slaughtered offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא begun in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונן may not bring an עולה, בכור, מעשר, פסח, חטאת or אשם.

steps.title: The ברייתא includes birds, meal offerings, wine, wood and frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The words שלמים קרבנו teach that any offering at all is brought only when the person is שלם, not when he is an אונן.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know bird offerings, meal offerings, wine, wood and frankincense are included? The verse says 'שלמים קרבנו'. Every offering a person brings, he brings when he is whole, and not when he is an אונן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last part of the ברייתא. It extends the rule even to things that are not animals at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זבח only covered slaughtered animals. The word קרבנו covers every kind of offering. The play on שלמים and שלם gives the reason: an offering is brought when a person is 'whole', and an אונן is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Bird offerings
Meal offerings, made of flour
Frankincense
Whole, at peace. This is the opposite of an אונן's state
His offering. Here it includes every kind of offering

steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, the פסח is clearly on the list of offerings an אונן may not bring.

phrases.english: From where do we include the bird offerings and the meal offerings
and the wine, and the wood, and the frankincense?
The verse says: 'peace offerings, his offering';
all offerings that he brings,
he brings when he is whole,
and he does not bring when he is an acute mourner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by including non-animal offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונן may not bring any offering at all, not even birds, meal offerings, wine, wood or frankincense.

steps.title: But the ברייתא lists the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that this ברייתא of רבי שמעון explicitly forbids an אונן to bring a פסח. That contradicts the ברייתא where he said an אונן eats his פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it teaches the פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the ברייתא it just quoted to challenge רבי שמעון's view. Here the פסח is named outright, so the answer from step 16 ('all except פסח') no longer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 the גמרא could say a general phrase did not include the פסח. Here the פסח is spelled out by name. So it seems רבי שמעון does forbid an אונן from bringing it. That would mean he treats night אנינות as Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. This points to the one detail in a source that matters for the challenge

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches Pesach!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in steps 17 to 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (step 14) that רבי שמעון holds night אנינות is only מדרבנן, so an אונן brings his פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא names the פסח outright among offerings an אונן may not bring, so the 'except פסח' answer of step 16 fails.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the פסח is listed for no real reason
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the פסח is not truly part of the rule. The ברייתא mentioned it only out of habit, together with בכור and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The פסח was mentioned for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge. He says the word פסח in the ברייתא is just there by habit and doesn't really belong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בכור, מעשר and פסח are often mentioned together as a set. So the ברייתא slipped in the פסח with the other two even though the rule doesn't apply to it. That keeps רבי שמעון's view the same: night אנינות is only מדרבנן, and an אונן does bring and eat his פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: He took it for nothing. The word was mentioned with no real purpose

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying the פסח isn't an offering or doesn't belong to its category. He is only saying this particular rule about an אונן doesn't apply to it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's view holds: night אנינות is only מדרבנן, so an אונן brings his פסח. Its mention in the שלמים ברייתא is just habit.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
Pesach, he took it for nothing.
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא named the פסח just out of habit, since it usually comes in a list with בכור and מעשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: פֶּסַח כְּדִי נַסְבֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word in the source is dismissed as mentioned only by habit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists פסח, so רבי שמעון forbids an אונן to bring it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mention of פסח has no legal weight; רבי שמעון holds an אונן brings and eats his פסח.

steps.title: רב ששת: 'פסח' means the שלמים of the פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת gives a different answer: the word פסח in the ברייתא means שלמי פסח, the שלמים brought along with the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: What does 'פסח' mean here? It means the שלמים of the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the contradiction from step 20. רב ששת says the ברייתא that forbids an אונן never meant the פסח itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the word פסח was there only out of habit. רב ששת keeps the word as meaningful but reads it as the שלמים that come together with the פסח. So the ברייתא forbids an אונן only from those שלמים, and he may still eat his actual פסח, and the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: The שלמים offering brought together with the פסח
What? (what is meant by...)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
What is 'Pesach'? The peace offerings of Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: מַאי פֶּסַח – שַׁלְמֵי פֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the contradiction that רב חסדא answered in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids an אונן from bringing the פסח itself, which contradicts the other ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only forbids the שלמים brought with the פסח; the פסח itself is still eaten by an אונן.

steps.title: Objection: that is just the same as peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if פסח means שלמים, the ברייתא already listed שלמים, so why mention it again?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's reading. If 'פסח' just means a kind of שלמים, it seems to repeat something the ברייתא already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole ברייתא was built on the word שלמים, so שלמים are obviously included. Listing 'פסח' as an extra item seems pointless if it is only another שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
That is the same as

phrases.english: If so, that is the same as peace offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's reading from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's reading of פסח as שלמי פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If פסח means a type of שלמים, the ברייתא would be repeating itself, since שלמים is the very word it started from.

steps.title: Two kinds of peace offerings are taught
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ברייתא teaches about שלמים brought because of the פסח and separately about שלמים brought on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: It taught about שלמים that come because of the פסח, and it taught about שלמים that come on their own account.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. It explains that 'פסח' and 'שלמים' in the ברייתא refer to two different groups of שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular שלמים are brought by a person for their own sake. שלמי פסח are brought only because of the פסח. The ברייתא lists both so that each is clearly covered.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of, on account of
On their own account, for their own sake

phrases.english: He taught peace offerings that come on account of Pesach,
and he taught peace offerings that come on their own account.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא שְׁלָמִים הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת פֶּסַח, וּתְנָא שְׁלָמִים הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning פסח is a repeat of שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two separate kinds of שלמים, and the ברייתא names each one.

steps.title: Why both kinds needed to be mentioned
steps.stepSummary: Without mentioning שלמי פסח, we would think they are like the פסח itself and an אונן may bring them; the ברייתא teaches that he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if it did not teach about שלמים that come because of the פסח, you would think: since they come because of the פסח, they are like the פסח itself. So it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא needed the extra mention. It shows what mistake we would have made without it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since an אונן does eat his פסח, one might think the שלמים tied to it share that leniency. The ברייתא lists them separately to show they are treated like regular שלמים, forbidden to an אונן. This completes רב ששת's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind to say (you might have thought)
Like the thing itself
It teaches us (otherwise)
Since

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ששת, an אונן eats his פסח, but he may not bring the שלמים that come along with the פסח. They are treated like ordinary שלמים, not like the פסח.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two: the 'פסח' in this ברייתא is not the פסח lamb. It is the שלמים connected to it, and only those are forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי לָא תְּנָא שְׁלָמִים הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת פֶּסַח,
phrases.english: For if he had not taught peace offerings that come on account of Pesach,
it would enter your mind to say:
since they come on account of Pesach,
they are like the Pesach itself;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תְּנָא שְׁלָמִים הַבָּאִין מֵחֲמַת פֶּסַח, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the distinction in step 24 is needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלמי פסח would be treated like the פסח and allowed for an אונן.
steps.terutzMaskana: שלמי פסח are forbidden to an אונן like any שלמים.

steps.title: רב מרי begins a third answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רב מרי, who will give another way to resolve the contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup: the גמרא is opening a third answer to the contradiction, from רב מרי. His actual words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two answers were already given, by רב חסדא and רב ששת. רב מרי is about to offer a different approach to the same contradiction between the two ברייתות of רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב ששת's answer to a new, third answer to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduction to an alternative answer (content follows)
